name: Misam
description: A star 35 parsecs away, 9.0 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 14668: radius 9.012 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 39.708 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.052) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 14668: effective temperature 4830 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.063)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 3.08 from 2016A&A...587A...2B; the 21 published values span log g 2.68 to 3.3, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 14668: distance 34.566 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.007), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 35 parsecs away, 9.0 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 40 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,830 K, so 9.012 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 14668: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Kappa Persei
quotes.card: Kappa Persei or κ Persei, is a triple star system in the northern constellation of Perseus.
quotes.introduction: Based upon an annual parallax shift of 28.93 mas, it is located at a distance of 113 light-years from the Sun.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 433103132037681536 (quality A), from 2005A&A...430..165F; Gaia DR3 measures none
